items.title: England hail ‘inspirational’ Lewis Moody after thrashing New Zealand
items.summary:
• Former captain, who has MND, was on pitch for haka

  • ‘Players jumped at the opportunity to support him’

England’s players have hailed the former national captain Lewis Moody as their chief source of inspiration after the record-breaking 37-12 Twickenham drubbing of New Zealand. Moody, who has motor neurone disease, joined the home side on the pitch for the pre-match haka and the current skipper, Maro Itoje, said his presence helped to fuel their outstanding performance.

Never in their distinguished history have the All Blacks lost by a wider margin to northern-hemisphere opposition and Itoje suggested a desire to underline their support for Moody and his family had been a significant motivation. “Lewis is such an inspirational man,” said Itoje, after his side’s fifth consecutive Test victory. “He was an inspirational player, too, and the players jumped at the opportunity to support him. He came to spend some time with us yesterday, presented us our shirts for the game and addressed us. There’s no doubt that him joining us for the haka and spending time with us gave us an extra lift today.”

Continue reading...
items.t: England hail ‘inspirational’ Lewis Moody after thrashing New Zealand

items.title: Alcaraz holds off Shelton to set up final showdown with Zverev at ATP Finals
items.summary:
• Spaniard beats American 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (1) in semi-final

  • Alexander Zverev sees off Daniil Medvedev 7-6 (0), 6-4

The man himself was not present in Turin on Saturday afternoon, but one of the most intriguing developments on and off court in men’s tennis this year was Ben Shelton’s surprise decision to hire the former world No 1 Juan Carlos Ferrero as his new coach alongside his father, Bryan. Ferrero is one of the most highly respected coaches on tour, but he also knows Carlos Alcaraz better than any other coach in the world.

However, there is only so much that anyone can do against one of the sport’s greatest talents. Shelton, the third seed, played a spectacular match, serving monstrously, attacking without hesitation and volleying well in decisive moments, but it still wasn’t enough to defeat the second seeded Alcaraz, who maintained his focus after an uncertain start as he reached the final of the ATP Finals with a 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (1) win.

items.title: ‘Fragile’ Chelsea must toughen up after Leeds humiliation, admits Xabi Alonso
items.summary:
Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon.

It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials.

items.title: England’s strength in depth finally comes together in landmark victory over All Blacks | Andy Bull
items.summary:
Record-breaking win suggests Steve Borthwick’s side are realising their enormous potential at last

Something’s coming. Oh yes. They will be able to hear its approaching footsteps in Edinburgh and Dublin and Paris and Cardiff, the tremors will ripple through Johannesburg and Sydney all the way to Auckland, where they will finally arrive sometime when the New Zealand public wakes up to find out all about what happened to their team here at Twickenham. After years of being oh so ordinary, England are on their way at long last to looking like the sort of team their depth of talent and wealth of resources has always suggested they ought to be.

When they beat Australia, everyone said how woeful the Wallabies were, when they thrashed Japan, all the talk was about how far the Brave Blossoms had fallen, but there are no caveats when you beat New Zealand like this. There’s no such thing as an easy win against the All Blacks. And no such thing, either, as a bad All Blacks team, even if this one’s a long way short of their best. It was a record victory, the 25-point margin eight more than England managed to win by in their famous victory here in 2012. Honestly, it could, maybe should, have been by more. England had…
items.t: England’s strength in depth finally comes together in landmark victory over All Blacks | Andy Bull

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI appears to mock NFL sexual misconduct scandals in radio parody
items.summary:
• Comedian Stavros Halkias voices fictional shock jock

  • Segment echoes Watson, Tucker misconduct allegations

  • Rockstar’s latest skewers American sports culture

The long-awaited Grand Theft Auto VI appears to have taken aim at the NFL’s sexual misconduct scandals – and the culture of excuses surrounding them – with a satirical segment on the video game’s fictional conservative talk radio station bearing striking similarities to allegations against Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson and Kansas City Chiefs kicker Justin Tucker.

The segment features comedian and voice actor Stavros Halkias defending Anthony Ross, a fictional player for the Vice City Manatees, after an “alleged” incident involving a team masseuse. Although neither Watson nor Tucker are mentioned by name, the circumstances closely resemble allegations made against both players.

Continue reading...
items.t: Grand Theft Auto VI appears to mock NFL sexual misconduct scandals in radio parody

items.title: Training hard and biding his time, Dele Alli has not given up on football yet
items.summary:
The 30-year-old former England star combines Twitch streaming with working to return to the top as a player

Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of becoming an internet personality.

He trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah. They spend four days on the pitch and days in between in the gym. A typical day begins at 9am with an hour of activation and stretching before Dele heads to non-league Windsor & Eton at 11am, where he trains on the pitches and uses the facilities. Then it’s back home to use his own oxygen chamber and sauna for a recovery session.

Continue reading...
items.t: Training hard and biding his time, Dele Alli has not given up on football yet

items.title: Pochettino the connector: will human touch lift Manchester United?

Argentinian has excelled in man-management – but will need his powers to energise new squad and impress owners

Mauricio Pochettino celebrated his 50th birthday in style. It was March 2022, he was in charge at Paris Saint-Germain and the venue was a stunning boutique hotel; the kind that many capitals have but only Paris truly does. Pochettino’s family and friends were there. So were his inner coaching circle, who are basically family. There were lots of people from PSG. And a good time was had by all.

For Pochettino, it was emotional. As everybody knows, the new Manchester United head coach is the kind of guy to well up when the speeches start, so imagine how he felt when he looked up at the big screen and a video montage of well-wishers started to roll.

items.title: Men’s tennis boosts prize money for players to more than $350m in major overhaul
items.summary:
• Cash increase via ATP’s creation of ‘One Vision’ company

  • More rest breaks added to reduce player welfare issues

The Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) has approved major changes to the financial structure of men’s tennis that will make the total prize money available to the players increase to more than $350m (£267m) by 2028, from $270m this year.

The creation of a new company to sell all the tour’s media, commercial and data rights, ATP Ventures, will lead to the investment of an additional $100m in player remuneration including an increased $50m bonus pool, a $25m year-end rankings bonus and $26m player pensions.

Continue reading...
items.t: Major changes in men’s tennis will take prize money for players to more than $350m
